Capabilities: 200 { capabilities[], machine_name, product, version } listing status, cancel, outcome, outcome codes, library folders -> asks and tells accordingly; stores the version
Capabilities: 401 { detail } (no secret sent) -> status: hand-offs are not judged and the connection shows "refused the webhook secret"; outcome: stays owed
Capabilities: 401 { detail } (wrong secret) -> status: Activity processing.status-forbidden, connection "degraded", hand-off kept; outcome: processing.outcome-delayed, owed, no outcome post sent

Library folders: 200 { libraries[]: id, name, media_type, watched_folder, work_folder, output_folder, manager_library_key, folders_from_manager, minimum_file_size_bytes } -> checks each library's folders against Weir's; a hand-off leaves out files under the minimum size
Hand-off: 200 { status: "ok", source, event, media_scope, enqueued } for a file -> hand-off recorded as submitted
Hand-off: 200 for a file not in the watched folder yet -> same; Weir's status then says what it found
Hand-off: 200 for a release folder -> same
Hand-off: 200 for a release folder with sourceFiles -> same
Hand-off: 200 for the same source sent again -> same; the older send's own report is settled apart (section 7)
Hand-off: 200 { status: "ignored", source } (no source path in the body) -> recorded as submitted. Deluno never sends a body without a source path, which the request test pins
Hand-off: 400 { detail } (no workflow watches the folder) -> hand-off marked failed with "The processor refused the hand-off with HTTP 400: <Weir's words>"
Hand-off: 401 { detail } (wrong secret) -> same, HTTP 401
Status: 200 queued with queuePosition (12, 6) -> stored on the hand-off and shown as the place in line; waits; no Activity line
Status: 200 working, message "Weir has claimed this file and is checking it now." -> stored and shown; waits; no stall until the library's limit
Status: 200 completed with outputPath and outputFiles -> stored and shown; waits for Weir's report or the output folder to bring the file in; never ended on the status alone

Status: 200 completed, outputPath null (Weir had cleaned the file for an older send) -> stored; for a hand-off that replaced an earlier send Deluno matches the cleaned file it finds at once and queues the import (processing.completed.import-queued); otherwise waits

Status: 200 failed, message (file under the minimum size) -> hand-off ends failed with "Weir reports failed for <release>: <Weir's message>"; Activity processing.failed; a case to clear is raised (processor-failed)
Status: 200 cancelled -> hand-off ends stopped, "Weir stopped work on <release>."; Activity processing.cancelled

Status: 404 { detail: "Weir has never received this hand-off." } -> inside 15 minutes of the last change: nothing (not believed). After: hand-off ends lost, Activity processing.lost, case processor-lost raised
Status: status of a hand-off read after a refused cancel -> as above
Status: 200 completed: a single-file source (qBittorrent) -> as above. **outputPath is flat in the output folder (<output>\<file>.mkv), no folder named after the source** (#1262)

Status: 200 completed: a release folder (Transmission) and a Usenet job (SABnzbd; Deluno names the file inside the job folder) -> as above; the output keeps the folder: <output>\<release>\<release>.mkv
Status: 200 queued, polled every minute while Weir is paused -> waits
Status: 401 { detail: "Invalid or missing X-Webhook-Secret header." } (wrong secret, or none) -> as for the capabilities refusal
Status: 404 { detail } for an unknown or malformed id -> as no-record
Status: 404 { detail: "Unknown media manager source 'x'." }, checked before the secret -> none
Status: 403 { detail: "Set a webhook secret in Weir so a media manager can ask about hand-offs." } (no connection of that source has a secret) -> as the 401
Cancel: 204 (still queued) -> hand-off ends stopped, "...and it was asked to drop <release>"; Activity processing.cancelled

Cancel: 409 { detail: "This hand-off is working, so Weir did not cancel it." } -> nothing changed; "Weir has started work ... Deluno will not interrupt it" (a removed title ends it anyway and its output is not imported)
Cancel: 409 { detail: "...is completed, so Weir did not cancel it." } -> same: nothing changed; the next status poll shows completed
Cancel: 204 as Deluno sent it: "Stop waiting" on a hand-off Weir holds queued -> as the row above
Cancel: 401 (wrong secret) -> nothing changed; the hand-off is not ended as dropped
Cancel: 404 { detail } (an id Weir never received) -> hand-off ends stopped, as if it were dropped
Cancel: 409 { detail: "This hand-off is completed, so Weir did not cancel it." } (a hand-off finished long ago) -> nothing changed

Cancel: 403 { detail: "Missing X-Requested-With header…" } (an Origin header with no X-Requested-With on a POST or DELETE; Deluno sends no Origin) -> not sent by Deluno; recorded so Weir's rule stays known
Outcome: 200 { handoffId, outcome, released: true, message } -> delivered, one attempt; processing.outcome-reported "... It released its copy."; never asked again
Outcome: 200 released: false (Weir's copy is the library file) -> delivered; Activity says Deluno told Weir it has the file and repeats Weir's own words
Outcome: 200, imported with a reason note -> delivered; Activity carries the note in brackets
Outcome: 200, not-imported, no reason / the default words / an import refusal -> delivered; Activity "Deluno told Weir it will not import <release>: <reason>"; Weir kept its copy

Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "handoff_not_finished" } (queued, working) -> stays owed: pending, next attempt a minute later, then doubling to an hour; Activity processing.outcome-delayed said once; gives up after a week
Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "handoff_ended" } (cancelled, failed) -> refused, one attempt, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-not-reported with Weir's words
Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "outcome_already_recorded" } -> settled, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-kept "kept its earlier answer"
Outcome: 404 { detail } -> "never received", not a failure, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-never-received
Outcome: 401 (wrong secret) -> stays owed; the connection is shown refused
Outcome: 404 { detail: "Weir has never received this hand-off." } -> as the row above

Outcome: 422 (unknown outcome word, missing outcome, a body that is not JSON; checked before the secret) and 415 (not declared JSON) { detail: [...] } -> the report was wrong; never sent again (Deluno never sends such a body)
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed with outputPath and outputFiles (a single file; a release folder; a Usenet job) -> an import is queued
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed for a release that was sent again -> the newer send settles from its own report
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed after the person stopped waiting (the hand-off ended dismissed) -> no import is queued
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed, file under the minimum size (disposition: "held") -> nothing imported; the hand-off ends failed
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed with failureClass: "source_gone" (the download was deleted) -> the hand-off ends as source gone
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed, a file Weir cannot read (disposition: "held") -> nothing imported

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { libraries: [] }, and 404 { error: "library_not_found", message: "Deluno has no library with the id <id>." } for a libraryId Deluno does not have (a 404 with no body means only that the route is missing, #1267) -> reply-download-destinations-empty

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { libraries[]: libraryId, libraryName, mediaType, downloadsPath, processorOutputPath, importWorkflow, destinations[], processorConnection }, with the processor connection and its pathMappings for a library that hands to a processor, null for one that does not; 404 { error: "library_not_found", message } for an unknown library -> reply-download-destinations-libraries
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 401 (no body) on each of the four routes, with no credential -> reply-no-sign-in

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: a key with only the read scope: 403 { message } on the two reads (the route's own scope check, "This API key does not include the required scope: imports.") and 403 { error, required, granted } on the two writes (the authorization policy) -> reply-key-without-imports-scope

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: a key with only the imports scope: the two reads answer 200 and the two writes pass the scope check (404 for an unknown id) -> reply-key-with-imports-scope-only
Every route checks who is asking first, then the size of the body, then its content type, then the body itself, so an anonymous caller learns nothing about a route's body rules

WEIR_LIBRARY_SWAP_HOLD_AT (tests only): a library swap stops for good at the named point so a test can end the process there; an unknown point is refused at start, and any value is refused at start when WEIR_ENV is production, so a real install never honours it

WEIR_PERIODIC_TASK_SPEEDUP (tests only): every scheduled task runs that many times as often (1 to 1000, never faster than every tenth of a second), so a browser test waits for the server's next look at a folder or a lapsed pause in seconds; any value above 1 is refused at start when WEIR_ENV is production, so a real install never honours it
